chosen_property.justification: The schema.org 'participant' property directly matches the 'SocialEvent → Person' signature, representing indirect involvement in an action.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: lender
candidates.comment: A lending participant relation between a borrow action and the person or organization providing the object being borrowed. Also called: loan provider, creditor, financing entity. Examples: "BorrowAction lender Bank of America", "BorrowAction lender John Doe", "BorrowAction lender Library".

candidates.label: superEvent

candidates.label: timestamp

candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: address
candidates.comment: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address. Examples: "A company's address is '123 Main St, Anytown'.", "A person's address is 'PO Box 123'.", "The restaurant's address is '456 Oak Ave'."

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: expressedIn
candidates.comment: An expressed in relation between a gene and the anatomical structure, system, or biological entity where its activity has been experimentally observed. Also called: gene activity location, observed in, found in. Examples: "Gene A" expressed in "Brain", "Gene B" expressed in "Liver", "Gene C" expressed in "Digestive System".

relations.definition: A connection or association between an entity and an organization or location.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: address
candidates.comment: An address relation between an entity (e.g., organization, person, place) and its physical postal address. Also called physical location, mailing address, street address. Examples: "A company's address is '123 Main St, Anytown'.", "A person's address is 'PO Box 123'.", "The restaurant's address is '456 Oak Ave'."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: sourceOrganization
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a creative work and the organization on whose behalf its creator was working. Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

relations.definition: The beginning date of an event.
relations.embedding_query_text: startDate: The beginning date of an event.

chosen_property.label: startDate
chosen_property.justification: The schema.org 'startDate' property matches the 'SocialEvent → Schedule' signature for temporal markers.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: jobStartDate
candidates.comment: An employment start date relation between a job posting and the anticipated date for a successful applicant to begin work. Also called start date, commencement date, employment beginning. Examples: A job posting has a jobStartDate of '2024-09-01'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'Fall 2024'. A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'as soon as possible'. Distinct from jobImmediateStart, which is a boolean flag for immediate availability.

candidates.label: applicationStartDate
candidates.comment: An application start date relation between an educational or occupational program and the date when it begins accepting applications for an enrollment cycle. Also called application opening date, submission start date. Examples: "A university program's application start date is '2022-09-01'.", "The scholarship program's application start date is 'January 1st'."

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: coverageStartTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage begins. Also called: coverage start, reporting start time, live blog commencement. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.

candidates.label: foundingDate
candidates.comment: A founding date relation between an organization and the specific date it was established. Also called: establishment date, creation date, inception date. Examples: "Microsoft" founding date "1975-04-04", "Apple Inc." founding date "1976-04-01", "Google" founding date "1998-09-04".

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

chosen_property.label: instrument
chosen_property.justification: The schema.org 'instrument' property fits the 'SocialEvent → PhysicalObject' signature for objects used during an action.

candidates.label: tool
candidates.comment: A tool relation between instructions or a direction and an object used but not consumed during the performance. Also called instrument, implement, equipment. Examples: "HowTo tool 'hammer'", "HowToDirection tool 'screwdriver'", "Recipe tool 'mixing bowl'". Distinct from instrument, which is a more general property for any object used in an action.

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: usesDevice
candidates.comment: A uses device relation between a medical test and the medical device employed to perform it. Also called device used, equipment for test, test instrument. Examples: "MedicalTest 'Ultrasound' usesDevice 'Ultrasound Scanner'", "MedicalTest 'ECG' usesDevice 'Electrocardiograph'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Pressure Measurement' usesDevice 'Sphygmomanometer'".

candidates.label: instrument
candidates.comment: A tool or means relation between an action and the object used by an agent to perform that action. Also called tool, means, device, implement, apparatus. Examples: A writing action uses a 'pen' as its instrument. A cooking action uses a 'knife' as its instrument. A painting action uses a 'brush' as its instrument. Distinct from object, which is the primary entity acted upon, not the tool used.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: usageInfo
candidates.comment: A usage info relation between a creative work and additional information about its use, including licensing options, citation conventions, or purchasing details. Also called usage guidelines, licensing information, rights information. Examples: "CreativeWork usageInfo 'https://example.com/usage-policy'", "Image usageInfo 'Commercial licenses available upon request.'", "Dataset usageInfo 'https://example.com/data-license'". Distinct from license, which indicates the specific license(s) applicable to the content.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: An authorization given to a specific entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: grantedTo: An authorization given to a specific entity.

chosen_property.label: grantedTo
chosen_property.definition: A permit issued to a specific place or venue.
chosen_property.justification: Minted 'grantedTo' as no schema.org property directly matches 'Permit → StadiumOrArena' for authorization to a venue.

candidates.label: grantee
candidates.comment: A grantee relation between a digital document permission and the audience, contact point, organization, or person to whom the permission is granted. Also called: permission recipient, authorized party, beneficiary. Examples: "Document Access Permission" grantee "Team Members", "File Sharing Permission" grantee "John Doe", "API Access Permission" grantee "Developer Organization".

candidates.label: permissionType
candidates.comment: A categorical attribute indicating the specific type of permission granted within a digital document permission. Also called access level, authorization type, privilege type. Examples: A digital document permission has a permission type of 'ReadPermission'. A digital document permission has a permission type of 'WritePermission'. A digital document permission has a permission type of 'CommentPermission'.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: issuedThrough
candidates.comment: A service channel relation between a permit and the specific service used to obtain it. Also called obtained via, granted through, service channel. Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.

candidates.label: eligibilityToWorkRequirement
candidates.comment: An eligibility to work requirement relation between a job posting and the text describing the legal documentation needed for an applicant. Also called "work authorization", "visa requirements", "employment eligibility". Examples: "Job posting eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'Must be authorized to work in the US'", "Job eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'Valid work permit required'", "Job eligibilityToWorkRequirement 'EU citizenship or valid visa'".

candidates.label: legalRepresentative
candidates.comment: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.

candidates.label: permissions
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the permissions required for a software application to function. Also called access requirements, app permissions, authorization needs. Examples: A mobile app requires permissions for 'full internet access'. A software application requires permissions for 'access to camera'. A game requires permissions for 'storage access'.

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: ticketedSeat
candidates.comment: An association between a ticket and the specific seat it grants access to. Also called "assigned seat", "seat number", "ticket seat allocation". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketedSeat Row A, Seat 12", "The flight ticket's ticketedSeat is 23F", "This ticket is for a specific ticketedSeat."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.
